thread.title: Market Snapshot: U.S. stocks set to ease back from records ahead of blockbuster week

title: Market Snapshot: U.S. stocks set to ease back from records ahead of blockbuster week
text:
Mark DeCambre 
U.S. stock benchmarks traded lower on Monday as Wall Street investors found few fresh catalysts to lift equities further into record territory amid a pickup in borrowing costs. 
A retreat for the main indexes comes as the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury TMUBMUSD10Y, +2.82% rose to its highest level since April 2014, while the dollar gained some upward traction, after hovering around a three-year low last week. Rising yields can weigh on appetite for assets considered risky like stocks, particularly as yields for bonds climb above those for equities. 
Looking ahead, investors await a key speech by President Donald Trump, an updated policy statement from the Federal Reserve on Wednesday, a monthly jobs report on Friday and corporate quarterly results from a batch of technology heavyweights throughout the week. 
What are the main benchmarks doing? 
The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.30% fell about 76 points, or 0.3%, to 26,540, pressured by sharp declines in blue-chip components Caterpillar Inc . CAT, -2.47% and Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.74% 
The broad-market S&P 500 index SPX, -0.31% slipped 7 points, or 0.3%, to 2,865, as so-called bond proxies, real estate, utility and telecommunication stocks, falling sharply. Those sectors tend to see selling pressure as bond yields rise, luring investors hunting for richer yields. 
The Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -0.22% declined 10 points, or 0.1%, to 7,495. 
All three major indexes closed at record levels on Friday , with the Dow Jones Industrial Average soaring 223.92 points, or 0.9%, to 26,616.71. The S&P 500 index climbed 1.2% to 2,872.87. 
Read: How the stock market has reacted to State of the Union speeches 
What are the drivers for the markets? 
After last week’s gains, traders appeared to be pausing and awaiting a number of potentially market-moving events over the next several days. 
Rising yields also complicates demand for equities, with the aggregate yields for the Dow at 2.1%, and 1.8% for the S&P 500, compared with the 10-year Treasury offering a yield at 2.7%, while the short-term 2-year Treasury note yield TMUBMUSD02Y, +2.13% was at 2.12%. Bond prices and yields move in the opposite direction. 
Consumer spending climbed 0.4% in December, capping off the biggest increase in household buying since 2011 , below economists’ forecasts polled by MarketWatch for a 0.5% increase. 
Meanwhile, the PCE index, or personal-consumption expenditures index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, edged up 0.1% in December. The closely followed “core” rate that strips out food and energy rose 0.2%. The rate of inflation over the past year slipped to 1.7% from 1.8%, however. The core rate, stripping out volatile food and energy prices, was flat at 1.5%. 
Wall Street has been watching sluggish inflation for signs of normalization. 
Check out: MarketWatch’s Economic Calendar 
The Fed will announce the outcome of its two-day meeting, the last for departing Chairwoman Janet Yellen, on Wednesday. The market isn’t counting on an interest-rate hike this month, but has penciled one in for March. 
The State of the Union address from President Trump will command attention on Tuesday, as investors look out for any more rhetoric on trade, after he last week announced tariffs on Chinese solar panels and South Korean washing machines. In an interview on Sunday, Trump hinted at retaliation against the European Union over a “very unfair” trade policy with the U.S. 
On earnings front, 125 S&P 500 companies are expected to report this week, including Apple AAPL, -1.74% Google-parent Alphabet Inc . GOOGL, +0.23% and Amazon.com Inc . AMZN, +1.50% on Thursday, as well as Facebook Inc . FB, -1.53% and Microsoft Corp . MSFT, +0.01% on Wednesday.
